## Design

### 2026-10-06 – I started by creating the files of my project, then I opened the schematic editor but it froze cause my PC is bad. I went on slack for a while to research then I edited the schematic sheet data and en

**3h**

I started by creating the files of my project, then I opened the schematic editor but it froze cause my PC is bad. I went on slack for a while to research then I edited the schematic sheet data and entered my project info, after that I opened the tutorial page and started following it. The tutorial had provided their own symbols, which I tried to import but couldn't, then I went on youtube to find a tutorial and found one. After that I successfully(took a few mins) imported the symbol in my schematic editor then start by adding ESP32 C3 microcontroller, I didn't know how to block a pin so, I googled it, blocked the pins and after that I added the button symbols, took a few tries cause it was crashing, and after that I added a OLED screen and at last I arranged all the schematics.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/43eafa3d-5137-4e1c-9535-d2d97ccbf592/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-08 – First of all, I opened my project and added an RGB light symbol to my schematic, arranging it with all the other symbols. I went to the tutorial page to see how  to assign symbols to footprints, then

**2h**

First of all, I opened my project and added an RGB light symbol to my schematic, arranging it with all the other symbols. I went to the tutorial page to see how  to assign symbols to footprints, then opened the footprint assigning tool but, I couldn't find the imported symbols there. After searching KiCad a little bit, I found the footprint editor and remembered that I had imported the symbols, but not the footprints.

I imported the footprints and restarted the footprint assignment tool. Then I noticed that my resistor wasn't labeled * 10k * as shown in the tutorial page. I researched how to change the value, and it turns out I just had to double-click and change the value. I did that and started the footprint assignment tool again.

This time, I assigned all the symbols to their respective footprints, including the RGB light I added on my own. Finally, I opened the board editor, but the footprints weren't loading. I will fix it tomorrow.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/08dab700-1d0b-4316-9f0b-ef5bc7694057/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-09 – I opened the board editor, but I couldn't find the "import from schematic" button. After searching for a while, I found it, but it wasn't working. I Googled why it wasn't working and found out that yo

**3.2h**

I opened the board editor, but I couldn't find the "import from schematic" button. After searching for a while, I found it, but it wasn't working. I Googled why it wasn't working and found out that you have to open the KiCad project manager to import it. Then I remembered that I had to make the RGB work, too. I started adding the resistors, but I got stuck, so I opened ChatGPT for help, and it guided me through all the necessary components.

After that, I assigned the symbols to their respective footprints, imported the schematic into the PCB editor, and started making a starbie. I arranged the electronics inside it, but when I opened the 3D view, the board wasn't cut. It told me to run a DRC. I ran it and found a few errors, mainly overlapping edge-cut lines. After I fixed them, I opened the 3D viewer again, and it worked. Tomorrow, I will work on the firmware.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/33465ac4-637d-49b1-b3d2-b421f227ed1c/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-11 – I opened the PCB editor and improved the star design to make it look even better. After that, I arranged the components inside the star, then I started routing them. I got stuck multiple times cause I

**2.6h**

I opened the PCB editor and improved the star design to make it look even better. After that, I arranged the components inside the star, then I started routing them. I got stuck multiple times cause I didn't know that the via feature existed. I was trying to route them all with just the front Cu layer. After failing multiple times, I Googled to see if a feature like that exists, but that dumb search didn't tell me anything good. Then I did some research on my phone really quick, found the solution, the "V" (via) thing, and started routing my board from scratch.

I went on the Hack Club brand website and downloaded some HC theme stuff that I can use on my board. I Googled cat doodles but didn't like any of em, so I got one from ChatGPT. Later on I dropped that idea too cause it looked bad. Instead, I added a plain text "Starbie" in a playful font, added some Half-Life branding, did some arranging, and that's all for today.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/e78f50ac-6b59-411c-8b1b-750112262d10/video.mp4)
